assessments.reasoning: The procedure section identifies transmission by value, reference, and name. Figure 5.1 assigns the value default to its value-type row and the reference default to every other row. It records permitted and illegal choices separately from defaults.

challenge.method: Would an array of value-type elements inherit the scalar value default, or could any procedure parameter use any mode?
challenge.results: The array has its own row with reference as its default. An object-reference parameter cannot use value transmission. The rule applies to the procedure table and leaves class parameters outside its scope.

limitations: Allowed explicit modes depend on the parameter kind. Class declarations are a separate scope.
Value-type parameter refers to the table's value type row. Explicit availability depends on the row, and class declaration parameters are governed separately.
